narrative.overview:
Administration extends Sufficit's public identity with a console composition: professional, secure, and direct. Red identifies brand, primary action, and points of attention; most of the screen stays neutral so contracts, states, and consequences can be read without noise.

Density is moderate and deliberate. Compact tables, persistent navigation, and diagnostic messages treat the panel as an operating tool, not as a decorative collection of indicators. Hierarchy comes from typography, contrast, rhythm, and grouping; color never replaces text or structure.
keyCharacteristics: rare red brand accents over light and charcoal surfaces;
compact Inter typography, with semibold titles and monospaced technical data;
white panels bounded by a thin border and near-flat elevation;
explicit, actionable states that never depend on color alone;
dense desktop that turns into labeled records on mobile.

rules.name: Rare Red Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for brand, primary action, focus, and small emphases; it never covers large surfaces or running text.

rules.name: Readable State Rule
rules.body: Every semantic color appears alongside text, an icon, or a structure that names the state.

rules.name: Short Scale Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce giant titles: the panel prioritizes scanning, context, and comparison, not editorial heroics.

rules.name: Data Transformation Rule
rules.body: On mobile, essential tabular data changes composition; it is not limited to shrinking the desktop table.

rules.name: Flat by Default Rule
rules.body: Borders and tonal contrast structure the screen; strong shadows appear only when there is genuine overlap.

rules.name: Functional Curves Rule
rules.body: The radius communicates the object's category: control, panel, or compact state; it is not applied as indiscriminate decoration.

dos: Do keep a single h1, a short description, and at most one primary action in the header.
Do reserve interaction targets of at least 44 × 44px and a visible 3px focus.
Do show loading, empty, error, authentication, authorization, and unavailability as distinct, recoverable states.
Do transform essential tables into labeled records below 768px.
Do use real contract data and keep secrets out of the interface.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing non-essential animations.
donts: Don't invent KPIs, clients, users, or states to fill the screen.
Don't use red over large areas, running text, or as a substitute for hierarchy.
Don't hide unavailability, authority, or consequence behind icon-only actions.
Don't introduce glassmorphism, decorative gradients, deep shadows, or partial dark mode.
Don't force essential tables to exceed the mobile viewport.
Don't expose tokens, secrets, exceptions, or full identifiers in logs and transient messages.
